gen-eater-gf-lexend: Lexend runs wide and open, a plain sans with outsized lowercase. Eater's spiky, dark letters sit above it like a growl, and the soft thread-like strokes below take the edge off without dulling it.
gen-eater-gf-lexend-deca: Spiky and a bit menacing, Eater's gapped letters hang over Lexend Deca, whose unshaded line and small capitals look tidy beside them. Scale the heading down and the menace thins out.
gen-eater-gf-liter: Liter's lines never swell or taper, and its lowercase stands unusually tall with wide mouths on every round form. Eater's slightly lighter horizontals give the heading a gnawed, aggressive edge against that smooth surface.
gen-eater-gf-mada: Mada brings a towering midzone and curves that refuse to close, so every word looks lifted and open. Eater is the dark, jagged opposite, and that clash is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-eater-gf-martel-sans: Martel Sans reads with generous openings in its curves and a high mean line running across each word. Eater adds a menacing, soft-contrast heading, and the plain sans body stays easy to settle into over many lines.
gen-eater-gf-matangi: Contemporary Matangi sets twine-like strokes of one gauge, with rounded letters left open and a hefty lowercase. And Eater's faint crayon-rough thick-thin rhythm gives the headline a dark, aggressive bite, which is the strongest quality here.
gen-eater-gf-maven-pro: Maven Pro reads with an open gap in the c and thin-looking letters that have no thinner parts. And Eater's visible thick-thin gap keeps the heading gritty, while the sans body glides on quietly.
gen-eater-gf-michroma: Eater looks dark and aggressive, with wide gaps between letters. Michroma gives each letter a wide berth and leaves daylight in its curves, so a long passage reads slowly, spaciously and with stubby ascender tips.
gen-eater-gf-miriam-libre: Miriam Libre has the weight of drawn wire, with an s that opens generously between its bends. Eater is best at menace, with gently modulated strokes and gaps; Miriam Libre is best at a sturdy, tall lowercase that stays friendly.
gen-eater-gf-mochiy-pop-one: Mochiy Pop One hangs its very large lowercase on a line like clothespins, with joins no thinner than the stems. Mochiy Pop One's laser-cut sameness against Eater's dark, slightly modulated strokes is the pair's strongest quality.
